leadIn.title: Lead-In & Context: Going To
leadIn.content: Future plans: Look at the dark clouds! It is going to rain. Next weekend, Sarah is going to visit her grandmother.

instructionCheck.question: How many minutes do you have to present your weekend plans to your group?

meaningCheck.question: Function check: What is the primary purpose of using Going To?
options: To express clear, level-appropriate meaning in structured context
To translate sentences word-for-word from another language
It is an obsolete form never used by native speakers
meaningCheck.explanation: Correct · This structure provides explicit grammatical function and clarity.

meaningCheck.question: Form check: Does correct usage of Going To require matching subject, verb, and modifier agreements?
options: No, agreement rules are optional in English
Yes, matching grammatical forms ensures natural, accurate communication
Agreement only matters in formal academic writing
meaningCheck.explanation: Correct · Accurate form and agreement choices prevent misunderstandings.

form.title: Form & Structure: Going To
form.content: Subject + am/is/are + going to + base verb. Negative: am/is/are + not + going to + base verb.

pronunciation.title: Pronunciation Notes: Going To
pronunciation.content: Spoken stress, weak forms, intonation, and articulation patterns for Going To.

controlledPractice.question: 'Look at those clouds! It ___ rain.'
controlledPractice.explanation: A prediction based on present evidence uses 'going to'.

controlledPractice.question: Fix: 'She is going travel.'
controlledPractice.explanation: The structure needs 'to' before the base verb: is going to travel.

controlledPractice.question: 'Going to' mainly expresses:
controlledPractice.explanation: Going to is used for plans, intentions and evidence-based predictions.
